name: Karaveeranathar Temple, Tirukkaraveeram
deity: Shiva as Karaveeranathar (Brahmapureeswarar), with the goddess Pratyaksha Nayagi (Karaveera Nayagi)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Karaveeram, near Tiruvarur on the Kumbakonam road, honours Shiva as Karaveeranathar — also Brahmapureeswarar — with the goddess Pratyaksha Nayagi. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, it takes its name from the karaveeram, the oleander (arali), its sthala vriksham, into which the sage Gautama is said to have merged in his devotion.

sections.history: Karaveeram, whose Tevaram name is Tirukkaraveeram, lies about 7–10 km west of Tiruvarur on the road to Kumbakonam, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later, and the lord is known here both as Karaveeranathar and as Brahmapureeswarar.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Karaveeranathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Pratyaksha Nayagi — also Prathyaksha Minnammai and Karaveera Nayagi — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the karaveeram, the oleander (pon-arali or sevvarali), from which the place takes its name.
sections.legends: The name Karaveeram belongs to the sthala vriksham, the oleander tree, and the sthala purana tells that the sage Gautama worshipped Shiva here so deeply that he merged into the karaveeram tree — so the lord is called Karaveeranathar, lord of the oleander. The goddess's name Pratyaksha Nayagi, 'she who appears before the devotee,' marks a place where the divine is felt as present and near. The name Brahmapureeswarar recalls Brahma's own worship in the Shaiva lore of the delta.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail between Tiruvarur and Kumbakonam include Karaveeram among their stops.
sections.experience: At Karaveeram the pilgrim finds a quiet oleander-named shrine of the Tiruvarur country. Before Karaveeranathar and Pratyaksha Nayagi, 'she who appears,' the visitor remembers the sage who merged into the sacred tree, and feels the nearness of the divine in a small Tevaram temple of the delta.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Karaveeram is about 7–10 km west of Tiruvarur on the Tiruvarur–Kumbakonam road, in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head, with buses toward Kumbakonam and local taxis to the village.
